# std::arithmetic::generic

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/std-arithmetic-generic.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

The promotion contracts of `std::arithmetic::generic`: the four `promote` methods on Nat and Int, and the `add` and `maximum` methods that use them. The oracle proves each contract for all Nat and Int arguments on the Core module of the stdlib fixture. The reflection step that identifies that module with the public checker's result is assumed.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/std-arithmetic-generic.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/std-arithmetic-generic.toml).

<a id="arithmetic.promote.total"></a>

## Promotion is total

- Property: `arithmetic.promote.total`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic::promote`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

For each of the four input keys, the selected `promote` body evaluates, for all arguments, to the specified pair, and its declared return type is `Pair<Nat>` for two Nat inputs and `Pair<Int>` otherwise.

- Example: For `n: Nat = 123456789012345678901234567890` and `z: Nat = 0`, `promote(n, z)` is `pair(n, z)` of type `Pair<Nat>`, and `promote(n, -7)` is `pair(int(n), -7)` of type `Pair<Int>`.
- Run by: `promotion_values_types_reversal_and_idempotence_execute_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/IndexedPromotion.lean): `VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion.promotion_total`
  - Premises:
    - the theorem concerns the module `VastitasKernel.IndexedPromotionFixture.checked`
  - Assumes: [Promotion fixture reflection](assumptions.md#assumption.promotion-reflection)
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `promotion_values_types_reversal_and_idempotence_execute_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)
    - [`VastitasPromotion.IndexedRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasPromotion/IndexedRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)

<a id="arithmetic.promote.values"></a>

## Promotion preserves values

- Property: `arithmetic.promote.values`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic::promote`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

Each component of the promoted pair has the integer value of its input, where a Nat n reads as the integer n.

- Example: For `n: Nat = 123456789012345678901234567890`, `promote(-7, n)` is `pair(-7, int(n))`.
- Run by: `promotion_values_types_reversal_and_idempotence_execute_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)

<a id="arithmetic.promote.same-type"></a>

## Same-type promotion is the identity

- Property: `arithmetic.promote.same-type`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic::promote`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

Promoting two values of one type keeps that type, the two values and their order.

- Example: `promote(-7, -2)` is `pair(-7, -2)` of type `Pair<Int>`.

<a id="arithmetic.promote.reversal"></a>

## Reversal

- Property: `arithmetic.promote.reversal`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic::promote`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

Swapping the inputs keeps the common type and swaps the components of the promoted pair.

- Example: For `n: Nat = 123456789012345678901234567890`, `promote(n, -7)` is `pair(int(n), -7)` and `promote(-7, n)` is `pair(-7, int(n))`.
- Run by: `promotion_values_types_reversal_and_idempotence_execute_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)

  - Assumes: [Promotion fixture reflection](assumptions.md#assumption.promotion-reflection)

## Idempotence

- Property: `arithmetic.promote.idempotence`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic::promote`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

Promoting the components of a promoted pair again keeps its type and its values.

- Example: For `ni = promote(n, -7)`, `promote(pair_first(ni), pair_second(ni))` is `ni`.
- Run by: `promotion_values_types_reversal_and_idempotence_execute_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)

<a id="arithmetic.embedding"></a>

## The Nat-to-Int embedding

- Property: `arithmetic.embedding`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

The embedding of Nat into Int preserves addition, order and the maximum: int(a + b) = int(a) + int(b), int(a) ≤ int(b) exactly when a ≤ b, and int(max(a, b)) = max(int(a), int(b)).

- Example: `int(20 + 22)` equals `int(20) + int(22)`, which is 42.
- Not executed: The facts are lemmas about Int.ofNat; no program evaluates them on their own.

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/IndexedPromotion.lean): `VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion.embedding_preserves_addition`, `VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion.embedding_preserves_order`, `VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion.embedding_preserves_maximum`
  - Premises: none

<a id="arithmetic.mixed"></a>

## Mixed addition and maximum

- Property: `arithmetic.mixed`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic::add`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

`add` and `maximum` on any two of Nat and Int evaluate, for all arguments, to the sum and the maximum of their integer values. The result is Nat for two Nat inputs and Int otherwise.

- Example: For `n: Nat = 20`, `add(n, -7)` is 13 and `maximum(-7, n)` is 20.
- Run by: `mixed_arithmetic_delegates_to_homogeneous_kernels_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/IndexedPromotion.lean): `VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion.addition_correct`, `VastitasOracle.IndexedPromotion.maximum_correct`
  - Premises:
    - the theorems concern the module `VastitasKernel.IndexedPromotionFixture.checked`
  - Assumes: [Promotion fixture reflection](assumptions.md#assumption.promotion-reflection)
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `mixed_arithmetic_delegates_to_homogeneous_kernels_in_both_modes` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)
    - [`VastitasPromotion.IndexedRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasPromotion/IndexedRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: The oracle evaluates the bodies themselves: a mixed method promotes its inputs once and calls the homogeneous Int method, and a homogeneous method calls its kernel. The theorems state the results, not this call structure.

<a id="arithmetic.reflection"></a>

## The proved module is the checked module

- Property: `arithmetic.reflection`
- Subject: `std::arithmetic::generic`
- Rule: [Nat/Int promotion](../stage1a.md#promotion)

The module that the promotion theorems concern, `VastitasKernel.IndexedPromotionFixture.checked`, is the Core module that the public checker `Indexed.LegacySource.check` returns for the stdlib arithmetic sources in `tests/fixtures/promotion.json`, and that fixture is what the Rust frontend produces from those sources.

- Example: The frontend's output for the three stdlib arithmetic files equals `tests/fixtures/promotion.json`.
- Run by: `stdlib_ir_matches_proof_fixture` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)

Claims:

- `reflection`: [Assumed](../specifications.md#assumed)
  - Evidence: [Promotion fixture reflection](assumptions.md#assumption.promotion-reflection)
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `stdlib_ir_matches_proof_fixture` in [`tests/promotion.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/promotion.rs)
    - [`VastitasPromotion.IndexedRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasPromotion/IndexedRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: `stdlib_ir_matches_proof_fixture` compares the frontend's output with the fixture. Building `VastitasPromotion.IndexedFixture`, which `VastitasPromotion.IndexedRegression` imports, compares the reflected module with a fresh run of the public checker.
